source_updates.title: Musical Source Separation Bake-Off: Comparing Objective Metrics with Human Perception
findings: Table 2 reports SI-SAR greater than SI-SIR for all four stems, resolving artifact-only as the stronger endpoint in this pool
Section 4.2 and the Figure 3 caption still conflict about sweep direction, so the interior curve remains verification_required
paper says reference-anchor spread greater than 10 while README and all CSV flags implement reference-anchor spread at least 5
implementing the paper literally as violation at spread at most 10 changes 359 flags, 65 permissive inclusions and 90 strict inclusions
the 5889 rows come from 209 sessions and 50 tracks; no participant-track clustered interval is reported
source_updates.revised_conclusion: Use artifact error only as the stronger published endpoint; do not choose a weight or threshold until exact estimates, code, QC threshold and clustered uncertainty are pinned.

source_updates.title: Spacing Out: On the Reliability of Binaural Music Source Separation Metrics
findings: Bi-SCNet versus SCNet changes both training domain and augmentation policy
stimuli are peak-RMS-selected ten-second passages normalized to minus 12 LUFS
the statistical unit for 96 pairwise comparisons is not clearly identified as condition majority or individual response
no participant-clip repeated-measures model, effect interval or multiplicity correction is described
public unmerged itd branch implements PHAT-beta but not masked GCC, listening data or trained Bi-SCNet artifacts
source_updates.revised_conclusion: Retain the metric-failure evidence but do not treat Bi-SCNet preference or significance as a one-factor causal result.

source_updates.title: Do Music Source Separation Models Preserve Spatial Information in Binaural Audio?
findings: dataset generator writes unscaled convolved stems but independently peak-normalizes only mixture.wav
stored mixture therefore generally does not equal the sum of stored stems
mixture-only normalization can confound training target scale, separation metrics and gain interpretation
source_updates.revised_conclusion: Treat Binaural-MUSDB as a synthetic benchmark requiring an additive null audit before training or metric use.

source_updates.title: Embedding-Based Intrusive Evaluation Metrics for Musical Source Separation Using MERT Representations
source_updates.independence: independent authors and metric method but reuses bake-off listener data for four-stem result
findings: MERT-MSE pooled SRCC is 0.65 bass, 0.61 drums, 0.73 other and 0.78 vocals on the bake-off aggregate
per-song MERT-FAD pooled SRCC is 0.66 bass, 0.65 drums, 0.69 other and 0.73 vocals
correlations pool songs across four model tiers without within-model or leave-one-model-out validation
point coefficients are reported without model-song grouped intervals
per-song FAD covariance is rank deficient when frames are fewer than 768 embedding dimensions
source_updates.limited_conclusion: MERT metrics are promising secondary intrusive diagnostics, not production gates; require pinned preprocessing, numerical stability, within-model and held-out-model validation.

findings: CSV flags exactly match a less-than-5 reference-anchor spread rule
paper text says a greater-than-10 spread requirement
paper-literal spread at most 10 recomputation retains 5368 permissive and 2281 strict rows versus 5433 and 2371 released
no objective-metric table or analysis code is included
1284062239-byte audio archive was not downloaded
unmerged itd branch adds PHAT-beta, Hann 0.5-second framing and fixes source CLI flags
framing code tests length modulo frame count rather than frame width and can mishandle non-aligned lengths
masked GCC, perceptual responses, training code and Bi-SCNet weights are absent
synthesis peak-normalizes only mixture.wav and breaks exact stored mixture-stem additivity
no root licence found and official demo has blank artifact links
no root licence, dependency lock, generated metric outputs or model revision hash found
MERT loads with trust_remote_code true and no pinned Hugging Face revision
audio is converted to mono 24 kHz 16-bit PCM before embeddings
ratings are aggregated with median although the paper says averaged
correlation code pools models and songs without grouped intervals
BSS baseline calls pass sample rate in a third positional argument that is not sample rate in current TorchMetrics documentation

knowledge_cards: Endpoint tables can resolve a prose-direction conflict while leaving an interior sweep unreproduced.
Quality-control thresholds are part of the scientific result and must agree across paper, README and flags.
A five-versus-ten-point anchor threshold changes both strict and permissive bake-off inclusion sets.
Conflicting record and README licences require fail-closed rights handling.
Pooling songs across model tiers can inflate metric correlation without proving within-model ranking ability.
An independent metric analysis reusing listener data is methodological support, not a listener replication.
Per-song FAD with fewer frames than embedding dimensions has rank-deficient covariance and needs stability checks.
Mono-resampled embedding metrics cannot certify stereo image, phase, bandwidth or peak safety.
Binaural-versus-stereo training is not a one-factor comparison when augmentation policies differ.
Loudness-normalized listening can answer preference while hiding output-gain fidelity.
Repeated participants and clips require explicit unit-of-analysis, clustering and multiplicity handling.
A mixture normalized independently of its stems fails the additive null and can confound training.
